chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man vowed to walk to the House of Allah (the Sacred Kaaba) but became unable to walk. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Let him ride and offer a camel, for that will suffice for him if Allah knows exertion from him.'

key_terms.بَدَنَةً: a camel (female camel used for sacrifice/offering)
key_terms.بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ: the House of Allah (the Sacred Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is the substitute for a Hajj vow of walking if one becomes unable to walk?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *al-jahd* (sincere effort) in fulfilling vows (*nadhr*), where physical inability transforms the obligation from an act of worship to a compensatory sacrifice. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that riding and offering a camel (*badanah*) suffices, emphasizing that divine acceptance relies on the individual's genuine capacity rather than rigid literalism. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic view that vows are binding but flexible according to one's actual ability, preventing undue hardship.
